questions.q: What does Azure Policy actually control, as distinct from Azure RBAC?
options: What shape a resource is allowed to have, regardless of who created it — not who can perform which actions
Exactly the same thing as RBAC, just with a different UI
Only billing and cost allocation
Network routing between virtual networks
questions.explain: RBAC controls who can do what. Policy evaluates resources against conditions and applies an effect, regardless of who created or modified the resource.

questions.q: What are the two core parts of every Azure Policy definition?
options: A condition to evaluate, and an effect to apply when a resource matches it
A resource group and a subscription ID
A username and a password
A billing tier and a region
questions.explain: Every policy definition boils down to an if/then shape: a condition (the 'if') and an effect like Audit, Deny, or DeployIfNotExists (the 'then').

questions.q: What's the difference between an assignment that 'floats' on a built-in definition's version versus one that's 'pinned'?
options: A floating assignment automatically picks up new minor/patch versions as Microsoft updates the definition; a pinned one stays on an exact version
Pinned assignments are always deleted after 90 days
Floating assignments only work with custom definitions, never built-in ones
There is no functional difference — both terms mean the same thing
questions.explain: Floating is the default and picks up definition updates automatically. Pinning locks to an exact version, which matters more for Deny or auto-remediation policies.

questions.q: What is an 'initiative' in Azure Policy?
options: A bundle of multiple policy definitions, assigned and tracked together
A single policy definition with no grouping
A type of RBAC role assignment
The Azure term for a resource group
questions.explain: An initiative groups several policy definitions so they can be assigned and have their combined compliance tracked as a single unit.

questions.q: Does an Azure Policy's compliance effect appear on resources instantly after assignment?
options: No — Azure evaluates resources on a cycle, and results land on the Compliance page after some delay
Yes, compliance state updates in real time with zero delay
Only Deny-effect policies update instantly; all others never update
Compliance state is only ever checked once, at assignment creation
questions.explain: Policy evaluation runs on a cycle rather than instantly; the lesson's example took a few minutes for the compliance state to populate on the Compliance page.
